question: What happens to the patient's muscles during passive range of motion exercises?

options.B: They tense up to protect the injured joint
options.C: They remain completely relaxed and do not work
options.D: They contract forcefully to assist the movement

explanation: During PROM, the patient exerts no effort and the muscles remain relaxed while an outside force moves the joint. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h1)

question: Who supplies the energy needed to move a joint during PROM?
explanation: Because the patient is passive, a nurse or therapist must supply all the mechanical force to move the limb. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h1)

question: A primary clinical purpose of performing PROM is to prevent which condition?
explanation: Moving joints passively keeps tissues pliable, stopping them from permanently shortening into contractures. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why does moving a joint passively help nourish its cartilage?

options.A: It pumps synovial fluid throughout the joint space
options.B: It stimulates calcium deposits to form on the bone ends
options.C: It triggers hormonal growth factor release in the marrow
options.D: It increases direct blood supply to avascular cartilage

explanation: Articular cartilage lacks its own blood vessels and relies on the movement of synovial fluid generated during joint motion for nutrition. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which condition is an absolute contraindication for performing passive range of motion?

options.C: A healed scar from previous surgery

explanation: Moving a limb with an unstable fracture causes further tissue damage and prevents proper bone healing. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h3)

question: What should a nurse do when encountering resistance during PROM?

options.A: Stop immediately and do not force the movement
options.B: Administer a strong painkiller and continue the routine
options.C: Ask another nurse to help apply more physical force
options.D: Push harder through the barrier to break adhesions

explanation: Forcing a joint past its natural resistance or pain threshold risks tearing muscles, ligaments, or joint capsules. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h3)

question: How should the nurse hold a limb while performing passive joint exercises?

options.A: Supporting both sides of the joint securely
options.B: Applying pressure directly on the joint line
options.C: Holding only the very tip of the distal digit
options.D: Suspended freely without any physical support

explanation: Supporting the limb both above and below the joint prevents undue stress and protects the bone and ligaments. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h4)

question: A nurse prepares to exercise a patient's leg. What is the correct way to handle the clothing and bed linens?

options.A: Expose only the specific leg being exercised
options.B: Remove all bed covers to see the full body alignment
options.C: Leave all blankets completely closed over the patient
options.D: Undress the patient fully to promote total body air flow

explanation: Dignity and privacy require uncovering only the immediate body part undergoing the physical procedure. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h4)

question: When exercising a patient's lower extremity, where should the nurse place their hands for support?

options.A: Under the heel and beneath the knee
options.B: Around the middle of the thigh bone only
options.C: Directly on top of the kneecap and toes
options.D: Tightly wrapped around the ankle joint line

explanation: Placing hands under the heel and knee provides safe cradling and control of the entire lower limb. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the correct directional approach when performing a full routine of PROM exercises?

options.A: Focusing solely on the dominant arm and leg of the patient
options.B: Starting with the toes and moving randomly upward
options.C: Exercising only the joints that look stiff to the eye
options.D: Systematically moving from one major joint to the next

explanation: A systematic head-to-toe or proximal-to-distal approach ensures no joint is accidentally missed during the care session. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the most reliable sign of distress in a non-communicative patient during PROM?

options.A: An increase in overall body weight
options.D: A decrease in room temperature sweating

explanation: When patients cannot speak, facial expressions and tensing of the muscles show that movement is causing pain. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h6)

question: A patient whispers that their shoulder hurts halfway through an arm exercise. What action should follow?

options.A: Double the speed to finish the routine much faster
options.B: Ignore the comment and finish the remaining repetitions
options.C: Push through the pain to loosen up the joint capsule
options.D: Stop the movement immediately and assess the joint

explanation: Patient complaints of pain mean the exercise must halt to prevent injury to the underlying joint structures. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which detail is essential to record in the nursing notes after performing PROM?

options.A: The personal visiting hours of family members
options.B: Any patient complaints or signs of discomfort
options.C: The exact brand of soap used during morning bath
options.D: The dietary menu selected by the kitchen staff

explanation: Documenting how the patient tolerated the procedure and noting any pain is vital for ongoing clinical evaluation. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is prompt reporting of new joint swelling after PROM important?

options.A: It means the patient is ready for full independent discharge
options.B: It signals that the room temperature is too high
options.C: It proves the exercises successfully increased muscle mass
options.D: It could indicate acute tissue injury or micro-trauma

explanation: Unexplained swelling or redness after movement can signify a tear, strain, or other injury requiring medical review. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h7)
